:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Evaluate the risk-neutral expectation to obtain the Black-Scholes formula and identify what each of the two cumulative normal terms represents.
- Confirm your closed form agrees with your binomial tree to a stated tolerance.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Evaluate the integral: the expectation of the positive part of a lognormal minus a strike, discounted. Doing it once is worth it because the two normal terms then stop being opaque, and the second one is the risk-neutral probability of finishing in the money while the first is that probability under a different numeraire.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Reconcile the three routes: your closed form, your binomial tree at a large number of steps, and a Monte Carlo estimate of the same expectation. Report the agreement and the Monte Carlo standard error. Three independent methods agreeing to four decimals is what makes the next three weeks trustworthy.
:::
:::
